title: Separation, Constraint Qualifications, and Cycling in Outer Approximation
summary: The outer approximation algorithm is a widely used method for solving convex mixed-integer nonlinear programs. While the algorithm is well established in theory and practice, certain assumptions underlying its convergence are rarely discussed in the literature. In this paper, we examine two such assumptions: that a constraint qualification holds at the optimal solution of each nonlinear programming subproblem, and that these subproblems can be solved exactly.
